records.new_gloss_en: entirely lacking something
records.linguistic_reason: Devoid is predicative and conventionally takes of; not synonymous with merely empty.

records.new_gloss_en: an agreement between opponents to stop fighting temporarily
records.linguistic_reason: Truce is a pause in hostilities, not necessarily a permanent peace settlement.

records.new_gloss_en: a small animal with six legs and a body divided into head, thorax, and abdomen
records.linguistic_reason: Insect denotes the biological class with six legs as adults; spiders are excluded.

records.new_gloss_en: a sparkling wine associated with the Champagne region of France
records.linguistic_reason: Champagne is geographically protected in many markets, unlike generic sparkling wine.

records.new_gloss_en: to become subject to an expense, loss, or other unwelcome consequence
records.linguistic_reason: Incur typically collocates with debt, costs or risk and does not mean produce generically.

records.new_gloss_en: a violent criminal or hired intimidator
records.linguistic_reason: Thug denotes violent behavior and can be a stigmatizing label; avoid applying it casually to groups.

records.new_gloss_en: arranged in the order in which events happened
records.linguistic_reason: Chronological indicates sequence by time rather than alphabetical or causal order.

records.new_gloss_en: a person who translates words from one language into another
records.linguistic_reason: Translator can denote software or a human; program and occupational senses merit disambiguation.

records.new_gloss_en: something that takes attention away from what one should focus on
records.new_gloss_zh: 使人分心的事物；干扰因素
records.linguistic_reason: Distraction is also the state of being distracted; stimulus versus mental state may need split.

records.new_gloss_en: to deliver a religious sermon
records.linguistic_reason: Preach also means advocate moral beliefs emphatically; figurative advocacy is separate.

records.new_gloss_en: a surprise attack made from a concealed position
records.linguistic_reason: Ambush can be a noun or verb; noun attack sense is singled out pending POS check.

records.new_gloss_en: a feeling of worry or disappointment caused by something unexpected
records.linguistic_reason: Dismay mixes shocked concern and disappointment; semantic range is closely related but needs examples.

records.new_gloss_en: a formal contract binding someone to work for another for a period
records.new_gloss_zh: 劳役契约；雇佣契约（历史）
records.linguistic_reason: Indenture is historically tied to bonded service; also means a legal agreement or deed more broadly.

records.new_gloss_en: taking place outside rather than inside a building
records.linguistic_reason: Outdoor is an attributive adjective, distinct from the adverb outdoors.

records.new_gloss_en: a person who unlawfully and intentionally kills another person
records.linguistic_reason: Murderer presupposes murder, not any accidental killing; legal definitions vary by jurisdiction.

records.new_gloss_en: relating to standards of how things ought to be
records.new_gloss_zh: 规范性的；涉及应然标准的
records.linguistic_reason: Normative concerns prescriptions and norms, not merely statistical normality.

records.new_gloss_en: an official examination of financial records or procedures
records.linguistic_reason: Audit extends to technical and quality reviews; noun/verb distinction warrants contextual POS check.

records.new_gloss_en: the front part of the body below the chest, especially the stomach area
records.linguistic_reason: Belly is an everyday noun for abdomen and may be colloquial compared with abdomen.

records.new_gloss_en: a return to activity, strength, or popularity
records.linguistic_reason: Revival can refer to faith, arts or health; return-to-vigor unifies the central sense.

records.new_gloss_en: a woman whose main work is managing her home and family without paid employment outside it
records.linguistic_reason: Housewife describes a role, not necessarily marital status in all modern contexts; gendered and potentially dated.

records.old_gloss_zh: 职责范围；汇款；减免/免除
records.new_gloss_en: the area of responsibility or authority assigned to someone
records.linguistic_reason: Remit also means transfer money or cancel a debt or penalty; homograph senses require split.

records.new_gloss_en: a device or program that imitates a real process for training or testing
records.linguistic_reason: Simulator imitates systems for practice or experiments; not necessarily a game.

records.new_gloss_en: to break suddenly into many pieces
records.linguistic_reason: Emotional shock expressed by shatter is figurative and merits separate sense.

records.new_gloss_en: a change to the opposite direction, order, or outcome
records.linguistic_reason: Reversal applies to decisions, fortunes or motion and implies opposing the earlier state.

records.new_gloss_en: the quantity of work or data handled by a system per unit time
records.new_gloss_zh: 吞吐量；单位时间处理量
records.linguistic_reason: Throughput is a rate, not simply maximum storage or total transferred volume.

records.new_gloss_en: a change made to something
records.linguistic_reason: Alteration is a countable modification or the process; clothing adjustments form a frequent subset.

records.new_gloss_en: irregular rises and falls in a value or condition
records.linguistic_reason: Fluctuation denotes variation over time, not monotonic change.

records.new_gloss_en: the act of leaving someone or something out or preventing participation
records.linguistic_reason: Exclusion denotes both omission and enforced nonparticipation; examples may distinguish social versus set operations.

records.new_gloss_en: a female reproductive organ that produces eggs
records.linguistic_reason: In flowering plants ovary means seed-containing part of the pistil; animal and botanical senses differ.

records.new_gloss_en: a persistent feeling of anger at perceived unfair treatment
records.linguistic_reason: Resentment is lasting grievance, not simply brief irritation.

records.old_gloss_zh: 骡子；运毒者/走私携带者
records.new_gloss_en: an animal bred from a male donkey and a female horse
records.linguistic_reason: Mule also refers to a smuggler and to backless footwear; distinct nonanimal senses should split.

records.new_gloss_en: of the same kind or composition throughout
records.linguistic_reason: Homogeneous contrasts with heterogeneous; does not mean merely similar.

records.new_gloss_en: a person involved in armed resistance against an established authority
records.new_gloss_zh: 叛乱者；反政府武装成员
records.linguistic_reason: Insurgent can be a noun or adjective; political framing and legal status depend on context.

records.new_gloss_en: speech or writing considered meaningless or uninteresting
records.linguistic_reason: Blah also works as an adjective, interjection and repeated filler; POS must be checked.

records.new_gloss_en: to obtain support, praise, or information through effort
records.linguistic_reason: Garner often collocates with attention, support and praise; general gather is secondary.

records.new_gloss_en: to repair and improve an old building
records.linguistic_reason: Renovate means restore to good condition and may include modernization, not merely repaint.

records.old_gloss_zh: 精神病性状态；精神病性症状
records.new_gloss_en: a mental condition involving a loss of contact with reality, often with delusions or hallucinations
records.linguistic_reason: Psychosis is a clinical symptom syndrome, not synonymous with violence or all mental illness.

records.new_gloss_en: likely to cause difficulties or harm rather than help
records.linguistic_reason: Unfavorable also denotes negative opinion or assessment; evaluative and adverse contexts may need splitting.

records.new_gloss_en: to express strong disapproval of someone's actions or behavior
records.linguistic_reason: Rebuke can be a verb or count noun; gloss gives verb sense.

records.new_gloss_en: to shine with many small flashes of light
records.linguistic_reason: Sparkle as verb differs from noun sparkle and figurative lively wit.

records.new_gloss_en: a knitted garment worn over the upper body, especially in British English
records.linguistic_reason: Jumper means sweater in British English but a person who jumps in other settings; dialect matters.

records.new_gloss_en: the finished edge of a sleeve around the wrist
records.linguistic_reason: Cuff also means handcuff or strike lightly; garment part isolated.

records.new_gloss_en: a short account of an interesting or amusing incident
records.linguistic_reason: Anecdote is a brief narrative, not statistical evidence; often personal or informal.

records.new_gloss_en: a reasoned response intended to refute an argument or accusation
records.linguistic_reason: Rebuttal is the counterargument itself, not merely an expression of disagreement.

records.new_gloss_en: to draw air in through the nose to smell something
records.linguistic_reason: Sniff may also denote a nasal sound or act of showing contempt; noun/verb and figurative uses differ.

records.new_gloss_en: relating to the Earth's surface, regions, or geography
records.linguistic_reason: Geographic and geographical are standard adjectival variants.

records.new_gloss_en: having good luck or experiencing a favorable outcome
records.linguistic_reason: Fortunate focuses on good fortune, not wealth or high social position.

records.new_gloss_en: relating to the nose
records.linguistic_reason: Nasal also describes speech sounds made with airflow through the nose, a specialist subtype.

records.new_gloss_en: to pass, as an amount of time
records.linguistic_reason: Elapse is intransitive and normally used with time as subject.

records.old_gloss_zh: 柏忌；幽灵般威胁；鼻屎（英式非正式）
records.new_gloss_en: one stroke over par on a single golf hole
records.linguistic_reason: Bogey also means an imagined threat and British informal nasal mucus; unrelated meanings require split.
